panel_comparability.label: NOT COMPARABLE AS A PANEL -- this is the most serious finding on the comparator
panel_comparability.evidence: configs/benchmarks/griddd_qed_lead_manifest_v1.json records that GrIDDD selects its own 800 from a pandas-shuffled ZINC-250k 80/10/10 split (random_state=42), and that the reconstruction of that selection has canonical_set_intersection = 1 against Jin's exact 800. GrIDDD's released exact list is marked 'exact_list_blocked' with five named blockers.
panel_comparability.consequence: COMPOSE's 446/800 is on Jin's panel; GrIDDD's 45.1% is on a panel sharing ONE molecule with it. Both panels draw from the same ZINC-250k QED-in-[0.7,0.8] population, so the comparison is population-matched, not panel-matched. The repo's own archived draft (paper_iclr2027/archive/superseded_2026-08-19/experiments_old_subsections.tex:97) already says 'not matched: a different source panel'.

A K=8..12 extension exists on the volume at 200/800 sources; the K=8..20 directory is empty.

does_446_respect_the_per_sample_rule.label: VERIFIED -- yes, at the returned-candidate level
does_446_respect_the_per_sample_rule.rule: never compare our SELECTED top-k against a baseline's ALL-SAMPLE rate
does_446_respect_the_per_sample_rule.finding: solved@k is computed as any(c['success'] for c in candidates_sorted_by_k[:k]) where success is re-derived from the terminal QED and similarity of the molecule each trajectory RETURNED. No larger pool is filtered down: exactly 8 candidates exist per source and all 8 stay in the denominator. 67.4% of slots are extinct and return the unmodified source, and every one is counted as a failure (MEASURED: 4,301 of 6,384).
does_446_respect_the_per_sample_rule.the_caveat_that_still_applies: each returned molecule is the survivor of a 32-particle twisted SMC run whose weights use the goal indicator itself (h_phi returns exactly 1.0 in the region) and whose particles absorb on region entry. The 8 returned are therefore goal-conditioned outputs of a search over ~4,714 property-evaluated molecules, not 8 unconditioned draws. This is declared in the protocol, is legitimate twisted SMC, and does not violate the per-sample rule -- but it is why the comparison is a task-performance claim and not an efficiency claim.

fail_closed_proof.positive: prepare --verify-only prints VERIFIED fail-closed, contract=951425eea1146f66, capsule_files=100, receipt=5af9bb0889cd0e2d
fail_closed_proof.negative_control_1: setting oracle_calls_authorized=1000 without re-hashing -> 'contract envelope hash does not match its payload', exit 1
fail_closed_proof.negative_control_2: setting oracle_calls_authorized=1000 AND re-hashing the envelope consistently -> 'contract is not fail-closed: oracle_calls_authorized = 1000', exit 1
fail_closed_proof.why_both: the second control is the one that matters. A chain that only checks its own hash is self-consistent by construction; the flag check compares against literal expected values and fires independently.

arm_a_seam.detail: modal_apps/hphi_h40head_ab_app.py:run_source imports rdkit.Chem.QED inside the function and reads REGION from module scope. There is no callable parameter, no scorer argument and no configuration object. The paper-era QED benchmark CANNOT be dry-run against an injected free scorer without editing a frozen file.
arm_a_seam.risk: a benchmark that cannot be dry-run can only be validated by spending its real run. That run costs 228.8 container-hours (MEASURED from the banked records' own 'seconds' fields), so a wiring error is discovered after the spend, not before. This is worth naming even though QED itself is free: the cost is compute, not oracle calls.

arm_b_seam.detail: ProgramQueryLedger(output, task, evaluate, budget=...) takes evaluate as Callable[[str], float]; run_program_campaign never constructs a scorer of its own. This is the same seam pmo_population_v1.execute_task uses.
arm_b_seam.gated_by: pmo_population_v1.execute_task itself is NOT reusable here -- it raises 'task is outside the PMO-v1 three-task lock' for any name outside gsk3b / perindopril_mpo / celecoxib_rediscovery, and requires scored_launch_authorized. The generic seam one level down (run_program_campaign + ProgramQueryLedger) is what arm B uses, with no frozen file touched.

interpretation.measured: on 34 paired sources, arm B solves 2 where arm A solves 22, at 1/202nd the molecules inspected per source
interpretation.disconfirming_for_the_new_controller: yes, plainly -- the current controller is far behind at this budget, and its per-sample rate is 274x lower
interpretation.what_the_result_does_NOT_establish: that the current controller is worse. The arms are matched on RETURNED candidates and unmatched on work by 202x, so controller quality and budget are confounded. Arm B's mean best QED (0.851) is close to arm A's (0.863) -- it gets near the region and rarely crosses it, which is the signature of an under-budgeted search rather than a misdirected one.
interpretation.what_would_decide_it: run arm B at a budget that matches arm A's ~4,714 distinct molecules per source, or report both arms as success-vs-work curves. At the measured 12.6 s per source per 41 scored endpoints, a work-matched arm B is ~1.2 CPU-hours per source, i.e. ~960 CPU-hours for the panel -- the same order as arm A's 228.8 container-hours.

arm_b_failure_decomposition_measured_at_.reading: the binding constraint is QED, not similarity: 58% of arm B's endpoints already satisfy the similarity floor, but only 0.68% reach the QED region at all. In 6 of the 9 sources where it can reach QED >= 0.90, it does so only by leaving the similarity ball.
arm_b_failure_decomposition_measured_at_.actionable_defect_in_this_arm_B_wiring: the injected scorer returns 0.0 for inadmissible endpoints, so 41.6% of the charged budget is spent on zero-scored molecules. FiberControl's own stated design puts feasibility in the SUPPORT, not in the reward; this arm was forced to put it in the reward because ProgramTask(kind='t4') -- the shape that carries a real support constraint -- also hardcodes sa_max=4.0, which is not part of this benchmark. A support-constrained arm B is the obvious next iteration and is expected to recover most of that 41.6%.
